verdict: Iron Mountain posted record revenue of $2.0B, up 13.5%, and net income jumped 49% to $129M as its data-center, digital and asset-lifecycle businesses grew more than 30%.

segments.name: Storage rental
segments.note: Renting secure space for paper records, data-center capacity and other stored assets — the steady core of the business.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Services around the storage: document digitization, secure destruction, data-center services and asset lifecycle management.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the global business.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of warehouses, data centers and equipment over their lives — largely non-cash.

opex.name: Acquisition & disposal costs
opex.note: $5M of acquisition and integration costs plus $8M of losses on disposing of property and equipment.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $217M on the company's debt, plus $8M of other expenses.

takeaways.title: Growth businesses are carrying growth
takeaways.text: Data center, digital and asset lifecycle management together grew over 30%; Iron Mountain signed 102MW of data-center leases in the quarter, 137MW year to date.

takeaways.title: Cash profit hit a record
takeaways.text: AFFO — the cash yardstick REIT investors watch — rose 17% to a record $458M, or $1.53 per share.

takeaways.title: Dividend raised
takeaways.text: Full-year guidance was raised, and the quarterly dividend goes up 15% to $0.993 per share, paid January 6, 2027.

footerNote: Net income attributable to Iron Mountain was $124M after $5M attributable to noncontrolling interests; the $0.41 EPS is on the attributable figure. Acquisition & disposal costs absorb a $1M rounding difference so the lines add exactly.
